discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI Innsbruck, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Peter Zoller and co-workers predicted in 1998 that bosonic atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model and can be driven from a superfluid into a Mott insulator. Immanuel Bloch and Markus Greiner observed this quantum phase transition in 2002, the first clean demonstration that a textbook model of strongly correlated matter can be built and controlled with atoms. This established analogue quantum simulation as a new way of doing condensed-matter physics. Greiner and Bloch went on to develop quantum gas microscopes, which image single atoms at single lattice sites. These have revealed antiferromagnetic order in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string patterns, many-body localisation and entanglement entropy. Zoller's theory, together with these experiments, opened a field now pursued worldwide, in which long-standing questions of many-body physics, such as localisation, supersolidity and high-temperature superconductivity, are answered quantitatively in the laboratory.
